page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 48 vCPUs and 96 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 24 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. This instance has dedicated CPU allocation, does not bundle local storage, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations show strong performance across multiple compute-intensive workloads. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a multi-core score of 17695.0 and a single-core score of 2142.0, with top-tier performance in image processing at 18505.0. It demonstrates strong capabilities in software compilation with Clang at 39655.0 and ray tracing at 51080.0. For cryptographic and compression tasks, the server recorded a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.98 GB/sec and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 277.22 GB/sec. Passmark CPU testing yielded a score of 54727.59, highlighting strong extended instruction and encryption performance.

The memory subsystem operates with a 2.0 GB per core ratio, delivering a read-only cached small block bandwidth of 3206.74 GB/sec and an uncached large block write bandwidth of 64.01 GB/sec. In LLM inference tests, the server achieved a top-tier text generation speed of 352.2 tokens/sec for a small 135M model, and a strong prompt processing speed of 205.4 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. The qualitative cost profile is optimized for high-density compute workloads where memory requirements are modest, preventing over-provisioning costs. This instance is suited for software compilation, image processing, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
